stickersText: I’ve always been proud of the fact that I’m not afraid to do things alone, Whether it’s going to a movie by myself, travelling the world or moving to a new city where I don’t know anyone .., Being alone does not scare me., But lately, I’ve been realizing that clinging to independence may actually just be a coping mechanism , Because maybe if I’m okay being alone, it won’t hurt as much if people leave.., And that’s not to say that independence isn’t brave, because it is., But what’s also brave, is admitting when you’re lonely., It’s brave to admit you long for connection, It’s normal to want a circle , And it’s okay if you don’t have one yet .., Because community takes time. , It takes intention and it takes patience , There isn’t a lot of value placed on community building these days .., But there should be. , Because put simply, people are the whole point.

stickersText: This is how you can safely travel to Barbados during the pandemic, Barbados opened its borders to international travelers in July, Each country is assigned a risk level which determines if and how many covid tests you need to come, Canada and the USA are high-risk so I had to get a test 3 days before and the day after I arrived, You an do your second test at a government facility for free or pay for private testing at your hotel, While waiting for your results, you can stay in any of these approved hotels and villas, I stayed at plum tree club so i had my own kitchen and outdoor space to use , After you get your negative test results back, you’re free to enjoy the island!, All restaurants, shops, and bars are open -life feels pretty normal here, With some of the lowest infections rates in the world, Barbados is a great option if you’re looking for somewhere safe to wait out the pandemic, They even have a new one-year visa for remote workers!, Follow for more content about life in Barbados ☺️

stickersText:
BARCELONA, A Day In The Life Of a NYer Living & Working Remotely , Today I woke up at 6:30am for sunrise yoga. If you haven’t tried it you need to. The sunrise at the beach was magical today., After that I hopped on a bicing and went for a beach ride before heading home to change and head to work. I took my usual nice scenic walk to my coworking office., I worked for a little then went to a cafe nearby for lunch. I usually like to do a menu which is super common in Spain. It’s basically a 3 course meal for a very reasonable price. All this was just 10EUR. , After that I met up with a friend and went to Barceloneta beach for a walk and stayed until sunset., I still had some work to finish so I went back to my super empty coworking office for a couple of hours., Finally I was starving so I met my friend and we went to Born for an amazing ramen dinner. That’s about it. , The work life balance in Barcelona is top notch! , A Day in the Life of 
a NYer Living & Working Remotely 
in Barcelona ✌🏾

stickersText:
My story of how I became a Digital Nomad (PART 1), I got fired from my agency job in NYC while I was living paycheck to paycheck.

I couldn’t afford to live there without a job, but I felt SO burned & I really didn’t want another corporate job…, All I wanted was to TRAVEL but was broke. 
I sold my stuff, got my security deposit back from my apt, spent a month working odd jobs, and booked a 1-way ticket to THAILAND., My original plan was to teach English but I ended up getting an amazing job editing a magazine instead!! 😎 (I NEVER would’ve been given that opportunity in NYC but in Thailand businesses need people with my skills!), My career took off in Thailand! I made friends from all over the world, I lived in luxury on the 27th floor with a private gym and pool… my life was glamorous AF (& really f*ing fun). , Then… there were 3 major tragedies at home 💔 I moved back to the US without a plan.  I tried to fit in, but living abroad had changed me. 

I didn’t know what I’d do next but I KNEW I wanted to keep my traveling lifestyle alive., After a few months of serious soul searching, I landed a new job that was totally REMOTE while I was on a 2-week trip to Costa Rica. I cancelled my return flight home, and stayed with my laptop. 

My digital nomad life was born! , Part 2!, Follow for Part 2!  👉🏻

stickersText: Do you want to become a digital nomad but don’t know where to start?, Here are 10 STEPS to get started today..., 1. READ this book to get inspired , 2. Visit the website ‘Upwork’ and go to job listings in your country in the last 7 days., 3. Look through the last 50 jobs and write down the skill requirements e.g ‘Social Media Management’, ‘Tiktok Content Creator’, ‘Video Editor’, 4. Pick 2 skills that interest you, 5. Spend 1-2 hours per day researching that skill on YouTube/ebooks/courses etc , 6. Put your skills into practise on a daily basis. Offer friends/family fiends etc or do for yourself (for free) - the goal here is to build case studies, 7. Build a profile on upwork - listing case studies/experience (your rates need to be low to start to get the algorithm working for you), 8. Apply to 20 jobs per day (set the location filter to world). You’ll see thousands of jobs listed everyday., 9. Go above and beyond for all clients so you get a good review. The Upwork algorithm is similar to Airbnb - good reviews get you more work/bookings., 10. Keep this process going, before you know it you will have 10+ clients all paying you $300-$3000/month, 10 STEPS to becoming a Digital Nomad 💻🌴

desc: Hi, I’m Nic and I’ve been a self employed digital nomad for nearly 5 years 🤓.  I chose this lifestyle so I could travel the world and live life on my own terms 🫶🏼 Before becoming a digital nomad I had experience in Retail Store Management, HR and being an Executive Assistant. Unfortunately, my job at the time wouldn’t allow for remote working so I quit and started gigging across multiple jobs, CV Writing, Personal Assistance and Copy Typing. However, I knew I wanted to become a Content Creator as I wanted to do something more creative with my life that complimented my love for travelling so… I started documenting my life here on Instagram 🤟🏼.  After a few years, I decided to start a YouTube followed by a TikTok and next thing I know I was able to make Content Creation my full time job 🥰.  I’m a big believer in not having all your eggs in one basket when it comes to generating financial streams so I also offer coaching sessions focused on Content Creation and Van Life as well as creating and selling eBooks. When I have spare time, I make jewellery and tattoo as well 🙃 If you have any questions about being a digital nomad, ask away in the comments below 🥰 @NicRoams @NicRoams  . . #v#vanlifed#digitalnomads#selfemployeds#selfemployedlifes#selfemploymentd#digitalnomadlifed#digitalnomadsw#workforyourselfv#vanlifert#travellerf#fulltimevanliferf#fulltimetravellert#traveleverydayd#digitalnomadlifestyled#digitalnomadgirlsd#digitalnomaden#nomadlifen#nomadictnomadstories

desc: I don’t support communism, in fact I hate it because that’s the reason why my grandmother had to escape Hungary back in 1956 with my mother in her arms through hills and wire.  However, the remains of Buzludzha are impressive not only for the shape and size but for the psychological effect it has on you as you’re approaching it and you get close to it. From the distance it looks like a spaceship that’s ready to take off and you can barely notice the bad state it is which can be only seeing once you’re next to it when you get to the top.  I will never say this is beautiful but I will say that it is on its own a good example of human legacy that hopefully never comes back again.  #bulgaria #solotraveller #digitalnomad #digitalnomadlife #digitalnomadlifestyle #easterneuropetrip

stickersText:
How I traveled the 🌍 as Digital Nomad PART 2, I got my first remote job offer while I was on a 2-week trip to Costa Rica.

 I was sitting by the pool on the phone with my new boss and he said, “as long as you have good wifi and are online when you need to be online, I don’t care where you are.” , I called Spirit Airline to see if I could change my flight to a later date & MIRACULOUSLY I got a full refund! Suddenly I was in Central America with a full-time remote job, no return flight… & a party I wanted to attend in Nicaragua!, The party was AMAZING. I couldn’t believe I didn’t have to go home after it!

I promised myself there was no way I’d F* this up & I’d do anything to be the MOST RELIABLE employee ever. After a month of traveling, my boss was happy & started giving me better projects., I moved on from Nica to Colombia. Then to Ecuador, Brazil… at first I was only SOLO TRAVELING but eventually I started  meeting other people who called themselves “Digital Nomads,” (I never heard the term before!), The more nomad friends I made, the more I felt like my travel lifestyle was sustainable… & it WAS.

I ended up living out of my suitcase for 5 years straight! I traveled to 60 countries while making good money & so many amazing friends., After years at my job I quit in the middle of the pandemic to help people become digital nomads too. Now I’m a coach!

I use my intuitive gifts to determine which remote business they should create & then guide them through creating their biz and setting up their own traveling lifestyle.

desc: When I was younger I always thought that traveling the world would be a massive expense. Yes it can be, but it doesn’t have to be! Then 6 years ago, I learned how to travel hack! Beating The banks at their own game, leveraging travel reward bonuses to your benefit. The theory is to use a reward travel card on things or expenses you were already going to be purchasing. For me I used it to pay off my student loans, renovation and material cost for my properties, but it can be used for simple things like gas. However, the number one rule is NEVER let the card incure interest, and always have the money to pay off the card. after I learned this, haven’t been able to sit still since! ✈️🌎🗺📍#tra#travelhackl#balitravela#realestateinvestingg#augustay#diylandlordg#digitalnomadlifestyle
hashtagNames: travelhack, balitravel, realestateinvesting, augusta, diylandlord, digitalnomadlifestyle
stickersText: How buying more real estate got me a 2 week trip to Bali , I purchased a distressed 4 unit property in Augusta Georgia , I pulled a travel credit card with a sign on bonus , I funneled all renovations and material cost through the card to meet the minimum spend , Then renovated , And renovated , And renovated some more , Once the renovations were complete, I increased rents , And rented each unit at market rent , Then got the points and booked the flight ✈️ , For my flight nothing was spent out of pocket , I did this same process with 2 other travel cards , Then used the points to book this Air B N B, When done right, It’s called travel hacking, Beating the banks at their own game

desc: Full time travel does not equal a vacation. It is easy to see full time travelers and digital nomads as well as people on gap years as taking just extended vacations these long elaborate trips where they are staying in nice places they are doing all of the touristy things and seeing the sites. What's important to know is that most of the time that is not the case, people that travel full time do so mostly because they are either already working still and are retaining a full time remote job or a part time remote job that funds this experience, or they are potentially working at the places they're traveling like working for the hostel or for a ski resort, or they've saved a lot of money, sometimes over the course of years to be able to afford the travel they are currently doing. Still though the truth of the matter is that when you are traveling full time unless you use credit card  Sign on bonuses and are travel hacking like I am most of the experiences that you are having are staying in hostels for extremely cheap not paying for expensive hotels like many would on vacation, they may have quit comfy jobs at home and are just living life. It is no longer a vacation it is your life, and that is why people traveling full time aren't spending as much every day because they're not as rushed to see absolutely everything in every place they have the time to take it slow, Eat at street food vendors instead of nice restaurants, take the free walking tours instead of the one's Trip Advisor recommends for a couple $100 And focus on local experiences rather than catered experiences to tourism. Full time travel is about the experiences and feeling the place in its most authentic way not about seeing everything that you can and spending all of your money.  That's my take anyway let me know what you think? And if you want to know how to full time travel as well then follow along and I'll tell you how!  #digitalnomad #digitalnomadlife #digitalnomadlifestyle #fulltimetraveler #fulltimetravel #travelforcheap #gapyear #gapyeartravel #vacationtips #travelfulltime

desc: Replying to @lisaserota  Here are all my budget travel tips and travel recommendations for someone going to visit Tokyo, Japan.  1st I would recommend  Going to all the different cities within Tokyo, Japan such as shinjuku shibuya asakusa rapungi and so on.  Then I would also recommend going to Tokyo Disneyland and sea, the studio ghibli museum, the Ramen museum, TeamLABS Tokyo and some of the more popular places like Sensoji temple, Tokyo sky tree, Tsukiji fish market, and the Imperial palace.  As for food I would recommend trying yakaniku and ramen as well as my favorite Japanese chicken Katsu curry, CoCo Ichibanya is great quick and easy for katsu curry but I may also recommend somewhere that isn't a chain that specializes in katsu curry. desc: T I P S 👨🏾‍💻 - A couple things I’ve learned in the first month of my nomadic journey.  1. Ditch the heavy luggage! - I found that packing light is a MUST when you plan to move around from place to place in a short period of time.  Starting in Europe, the buildings are much older and you might find yourself staying on the 3rd or 4th floor with no elevator through multiple cities. Carrying that 50lb hard side will get exhausting even when just trying to pull it along the old stone roads. Once you get comfortable you won’t wear most of what you bring anyhow so PACK LIGHT, trust me 🙏🏾 2. It might get lonely - You’re solo-traveling so of course you know you’re going to be alone, but feeling lonely is a totally different thing to prepare for.  It’s bound to happen especially if you visit smaller cities where some of the popular apps to meet people aren’t as widely used.  I found that booking a tour of the city or food tour can be a great way to meet others and help feel less alone on your trip.  Also, just getting outside and being around the locals by working at a cafe or having a drink a bar can get you out of a rut if you find yourself in one.  These are just a couple things I’ve learned so far.  I’ll continue to share more tips as I continue to travel 👨🏾‍💻 What questions do you have about the nomad life or solo-traveling ? hashtagNames: summer22, moveabroad, traveltiktok, travellife, foryou, greece
stickersText:
So yesterday I moved to Greece from the UK and it’s undoubtedly the best choice I’ve ever made. 
I basically get paid to live here, I have my own 2 bedroom apartment to myself, the beach and ocean is at the end of my road. All my food is included and my landlord owns 3 rescue dogs that always want a cuddle.
Every morning breakfast is made for me and I can go swimming before I even start my day. and I can sit on the beach and watch the sunset every night.
I’ve already made so many friends and I start my new job tomorrow. 
At 19 this is the life I’ve always dreamt of and it’s completely and utterly the best teenage dream I could ask for.

Maailmanympärimatkalla
Etappi 1
Maa Englanti
Kaupunki Lontoo, Lunta tuli ehkä pari senttiä, Vuoroja oltiin peruttu ja osa reiteistä lyhennetty, Lunta oli meidän matkan aikana kolmena päivänä seitsemästä, Bussit kulki normaalisti. Busseissa oli kylmä verrattuna kotimaisiin, sekä ikkunat huurustui paljon., Välillä sai olla metrossa ihan kahdestaan ja välillä oli niin paljon porukkaa, että sardiinilla on purkissaan väljät oltavat, Julkisissa oli erilaista Suomeen verrattuna, että pystyit portilla maksamaan itsesi sisään pankkikortilla ja samallalailla kirjaamaan itsesi ulos. Näin ei tarvinnut ostaa erillistä bussikorttia., Täytyy antaa Suomen julkisen verkon toiminnalle krediittiä, siellä ei ihan parista sentistä lunta hätkähdetä. , Ei yhtään ihmetellä, miksi vaikkapa Lontoosta tullaan Suomeen ottamaan oppia lentokentän toimintavarmuudesta lumisateen aikana., Seuraa meidän matkaa 👇

desc: 🚐Spend the day with us - Van life South Africa 🇿🇦  Today we woke up at a beautiful lakeside campsite called SwartVlei in Sedgefield 🙌 We made coffee, breakfast, cleaned the van and had a shower 🚿  Today we are off to explore some natural pools so we packed snacks and took a walk to the beachfront 🌊  Once at the beach we found a spot in the shade and setup our picnic- we tried the Harissa Hummus from Mama Alles 🥰 You just add water and stir! It was absolutely delicious guys, 10/10 😍😍 After our picnic we swam and explored the natural pools, we saw so many gosh and even a starfish ⭐️ Then it was time to head home 🚐  When we got back we filled our water tank, cleaned the dishes and cooked an early dinner 🍲  Tonight we had Moroccan Tagine from @Mama Alles  😍😍 You just add hot water to the bag or pot and in 10 minutes have a delicious meal 🙌  We ate dinner outside then had a call with family ♥️ Afterwards we drove to a spot to watch the sunset 🌅  Then it was time for snacks, netflix, brushing our teeth and heading to bed 😴  Thanks so much for watching ♥️🥰 If you are looking for super delicious convenient meals made with fresh ingredients check our @mama_alles 😍 Perfect healthy on the go meals for any occasion 🙌💗 - - - - #safyp🇿🇦 #🇿🇦 #viralsouthafrica #vanlifesouthafrica #dayinthelife #digitalnomad #travel

desc: Working as a digital nomad in Antigua and Barbuda has the following benefits: •Easy internet access. With an internet speed fixed 20.95 Mbps and mobile 33.80 Mbps, you can work in any part of the world from Antigua & Barbuda, feeling at home or office. •Smooth visa application process. Applying for the Antigua & Barbuda digital nomad visa is fairly easy, and everything is done online. Moreover, you will have to wait only 14 days for an answer. •Tax exemption. As a digital nomad, you are exempt from ping income taxes in Antigua and Barbuda. •Warm climate. With a tropical savannah climate, Antigua & Barbuda has pleasing year-round weather. The best time to visit Antigua & Barbuda is November to April, when it is least rainy and hot. •Delicious cuisine. Antigua & Barbuda has become a food destination because of its fresh seafood, flavored dishes, and top-notch rum. This place is a haven for rum distilleries and sugar plantations. •Leisure activities. In Antigua & Barbuda, you can enjoy a variety of activities. Among the activities you can enjoy are exploring rainforests, swimming with stingrays, biking, kayaking, diving, snorkeling, sailing, and fishing. desc: People always tell me how they want to travel like me or have my life, and I have two things to say to that: 1. My life isn't all that you see on social media. There's a lot (both good and bad) that I don't post here. I have my issues, just like anyone else. But perhaps most importantly, I don't travel as much as it looks like on social media. Don't get me wrong, I travel a lot, but as an aspiring content creator I have to post travel content on a daily basis, several times a day, across multiple platforms. I can assure you I don't travel every day, or every week or every month. 2. Everyone comes from a different background and I've been very lucky when it comes to travel. I'm not going to sit here and deny my priviledge.  That said, no one handed this life to me. The content creation, solo travel and potentially being a full-time traveler, that was all me. It all started with a decision to change the way I lived and take risks in order to pursue what I wanted. And more importantly, action followed that decision. That is the most important thing. #travellife #travellifestyle #travellife✈️ #digitalnomad #digitalnomadlife #digitalnomadlifestyle #digitalnomadtravel

desc: 🤯 I quit my office job 5 years ago and this is what my life looks like now 🤯 Yes, I still work, I just don’t live to work, I work to live 🙌🏼. Meaning my work, works around the life I want. A life where I feel as free as I can and in control of how I spend it 🫶🏼 When I was working my office job, I never understood how people made the leap, I’m going to admit it 😬… I thought wealth played a huge factor in it. But 5 years down the line I can promise you it doesn’t. When I started this life I was in debt, I had -£3000 in my bank. I was living in London, renting a flat in zone 2 and felt like I was grafting with no reward. The world I was living in was eating away my money, my freedom and my soul.  So I made huge changes, ones that I had no idea would work at the time and ones that scared the hell out of me.  But I can tell you right now, I’m so f**king grateful for past me… feeling very Snoop Dogg right now when he thanks himself for his hard work 😂. But we should all be proud of the choices we have made especially when it works out! The changes weren’t an overnight thing but this is how I basically did it 🧚‍♀️  1. I got a remote job in my evenings whilst working full time 2. I bought a van to become my home 3. When the van was done I quit my office job and left renting, the income from my remote job was enough to keep the wheels rolling and pay off the debt I had accumulated  4. With my spare hours, I enjoyed life and started the business I wanted to do, become a Content Creator There were a lot of hurdles along the way, it really isn’t as simple as a list but if you want it, keep your mind focused and take every challenge as a lesson 🫶🏼 I love helping you guys tread your own path so if you have any questions ask away in the comments below 👇🏽 @NicRoams @NicRoams  #dig#digitalnomadlifem#nomadlivingg#digitalcreatorst#alternativelifestylev#livingontheroadv#livinginavanl#fulltimetravellerm#nomadictn#vanlifera#travellerlifeg#digitalnomadlifestylem#nomadgirlsngirlsrule

desc: Email I send after an interview when I don’t get the job. It’s easy to take rejection personally But there are many reasons why you don’t get a job 1. Maybe the budget was cut and they lost the position 2. They could have promoted someone or demoted someone already at the company 3. Or Maybe they gave the job to someone else and that person quit after 1 week Either way, an email like this keeps your options open.  Email: Good afternoon, I want to thank you for your time on Monday. It was a pleasure getting to learn more about the company during the interview process.  Although I was disappointed to hear that I was not selected for the position, I do trust in your leadership when selecting the best fit candidate. If anything with this position changes or you feel I would be a suitable candidate for another role at your company, I would be happy to come back for additional consideration. desc: Would you take a helicopter from the airport instead of a taxi?? During my last visit to New York City, I got stuck in a taxi for over two hours from the airport to Manhattan 🤯🫣 plus it was almost $200 I heard about helicopters that can do it in under FIVE minutes, for around the same price, so I thought I would try it! My first ride was $195, and $50 bucks off (I know a code for first timers) so it was the same price as Uber, but a fraction of the time.  Carry on bag is free, checked costs a hefty extra.  The lounge came with free drinks, the 5-min ride had the most breathtaking views of the city, and I was shocked at how smooth and quick everything was 😍😍 This saved me a ton of time and I would do it again in a heartbeat, especially if my flight was coming in or departing around rush-hour. * * * * #helicopter #blade #travellife #avgeek  #nycviews #helicopterride #travelhacks #traveltips #nyctips

stickersText: Älä mene tänne Vietnamissa, mikäli sulla on ahtaanpaikankammo ja pelkäät skorpioneja!, Käytiin tutustumassa Cu Chi tunneleihin, joita Vietkong käytti Vietnamin sodassa. Tunnelit sijaitsee noin 1h ajomatkan päässä Vietnamin suurimmasta kaupungista Ho Chi Minh Citystä, Päästiin kulkemaan tunneleiden sisällä, niitä on levennetty turisteja varten ja siltikin tuntu ahtaalta, Jenna mahtui kulkemaan kyyryssä, mutta Juhon piti kontata kun on sen verran pitkä , Tunneleissa ja viidakossa oli sodan aikana paljon rottia, käärmeitä, skorpioneja ja tulimuurahaisia, Tunneleissa tulee kuulemma  toisinaan vieläkin vastaan skorpioneja, Tiesitkö että amerikkalaiset polttivat valtaosan alueen viidakosta, jotta pääsivät kulkemaan paremmin alueella?, Meille esiteltiin myös Vietkongin sodassa käyttämiä ansoja , Ansoja oli monenlaisia ja tämmöiseen astuneelle oli tiedossa pahimmillaan pitkä ja hidas kuolema, Tunneleita käytettiin yli kymmenen vuoden ajan ja ne kaivettiin käsin, yhteensä noin 250km useaan eri tasoon., Täällä pääsi myös ampumaradalle ampumaan sodassa käytetyillä aseilla, Vaihtoehtoina oli mm. AK-47, M16, Colt 45, jne, Luodeista piti maksaa erikseen, Sitten mentiin ampumaradalle, Juho ampui AK-47:lla, Tämä oli suomalaiselle jotenkin erikoinen mahdollisuus, ei tiedetä että Suomessa ois tälläistä jonku nähtävyyden yhteydessä , Voi kyllä rehellisesti sanoa ettei tuolla ois ite selvinny päivääkään 🥵😬, Paina ❤️ ja laita tili seurantaan!

Kaupunki Bangkok, Thaimaassakin on kallista! Mutta mikä?

stickersText:
Paljonko maksaa halvin julkinen Hua Hinistä Bangkokiin ja kuinka kauan siinä kestää?, Maailmanympärimatkalla🌏Etappi 2 
Maa Thaimaa
Kaupunki Hua Hin/Bangkok, Lähdettiin Hua Hinin rautatieasemalta paikallisjunalla Bangkokiin, joka on paikallisille ilmainen 😲, Juna lähti 14.30, Hattuhyllylle meni niukasti isot 🧳 muistaakseni HSL paikallisjunissa ei mahdu ylös isot 🧳, Sitten paikalle tuli Jennan puhdistuspartio, kieltämättä juna oli hieman likainen, Ite juna on hieman askeettisempi entä HSL lähijunat, Liput maksoi 1,19€/hlö. Lipuntarkastajalla oli ihan perinteinen rei’ityskone 😃, Matkalla nähtiin mm. lehmiä laiduntamassa ja ne pääsi vapaasti kulkeen, niiden kohdalla juna aina hidasti, ettei kukaan jää alle, mikäli innostuu kirmaamaan radan toiselle puolelle, Nähtiin riisipeltoja, Matka oli pitkä ja aurinkokin ehti laskea ennen kuin päästiin Bangkokiin, Saavuttiin Bangkokin rautatieasemalle 20.45, 25min myöhässä, Matka kesti siis 5h25min ja n.240km. , Otettiin Grab hotellille. Matka 14km ja maksoi 7,31€, eli se maksoi enemmän entä junamatka 😅, Check in ja kamat huoneeseen, Lopuksi käytiin hakemassa 7-Elevenistä vettä ja vähä ruokaa, Tämä kulkukissa ei meinannut uskoa todeksi kun Juho antoi sille paistettua kanaa, jota osti myyntikojusta, Paina ❤️ ja ota tili seurantaan, Kuinka halvalla voi päästä Hua Hinistä Bangkokiin?

desc: [Freelancing Life] Besides doing a 9 to 5 job, I also have some freelance jobs as my additional income. Doing a freelance job while also having a full-time job mengharuskan saya untuk mengorbankan beberapa hal, seperti waktu tidur yang akhirnya lebih sedikit, waktu weekend, dan kesenangan masa muda lainnya. Beberapa minggu ini saya coba mengubah pola kerja saya, dari yang sebelummya kerja sampai larut setelah selesai full-time, menjadi kerja lebih pagi sebelum full-time. I try to sleep as early as possible setelah selesai kerjaan full-time, kemudian bangun lebih pagi untuk ngerjain side project or freelance job. Tantangan untuk terus belajar hal baru seringkali datang dari freelance job and for me this is my chance to sharpen my skills. For me, selagi masih muda, selagi energi nya masih banyak dan otak nya masih kuat untuk belajar hal-hal baru, mengorbankan kesenangan-kesenangan jangka pendek bukanlah hal yang perlu disesali. Miten thaimaalainen ruokakauppa eroaa suomalaisesta? 🇹🇭🇫🇮
, Maailmanympärimatkalla
Etappi 2 🌏
Maa Thaimaa
Kaupunki Hua Hin, Ruokakauppa-haahuilija 
on irti! Tällä kertaa ruokakaupassa 
Thaimaassa 🇹🇭, Meidän lähikauppa Hua Hinissä on Lotus’s, Heti alkuun on raikkaan näköinen hevi-osasto 🥥🥦, Kuten Vietnamissa myös täällä on oma tuotteiden punnitsija , Tuoretta kookosta myynnissä 🥥, Dragonfruit eli pitaya eli lohikäärmehedelmä on Thaimaassa suosittu , Suomessa ei olla törmätty irtovalkosipulinkynsiin, tämä on ollut meidän mielestä kätevä, etenkin jos on jossain paikassa vain vähän aikaa, Tämä oli freesin näkönen!, Salaattibaari löyty myös täältä, mutta täytteet oli erilaisia mitä Suomessa 🥗, Kätevä napata välipalaksi mukaan valmiiksi pilkottuja hedelmiä, Mitäs seuraavaksi keksitään?, Siellä se haahuilija on vauhdissa, tällä kertaa tutkittiin nuudelipakettien eroja… 😅, Kärsivällisyys ei oo Jennan hyve 🙈, Okei, päästiin eteenpäin! Vissyä on aina pakko saada , Suomesta ei taida ilmalämpöpumppuja löytyä ruokakaupoista. Näitäkin piti aikansa ihastella, Tiesitkö että Thaimaa on maailman suurin riisintuottajamaa? Riisiä myytiinkin vähän isommissa säkeissä eli 5 kg säkeissä, Okei, nyt jäin ite kiinni haahuilusta 🤭 apteekkituotteiden hylly oli kiinnostava , Tiikeribalsami lähti mukaan ja se onki tullu tarpeeseen hyttysten puremiin, Tää oli jännä! Kasvomaskeihin tuoksua, Takaisin ruokiin! Valmisruoka-annoksia oli tarjolla , Tää lihaosasto oli aika erilainen, Jenna kasvissyöjänä skippasi aina osaston kokonaan kun ei tehny mieli katella näitä 🥩, Täälläkin oli oma punnitsija, Eli lihaa myytiin ihan irtona, muovipussiin vaan haluama määrä ja sitten puntarille, Myynnissä oli mm. kanan kynsiä, Juho on sekasyöjä niin hän osti täältä kanaa ja vatsavaivoiltakin vältyttiin, Lihahyllyn jälkeen pakasteesta löyty kasvissyöjälle muutamia proteiininlähteitä, Ja loppuun suomalaisille samaistuttavaa! Thaimaassa on myös aikarajoitukset alkoholinmyynnille 🍷⏱️, Sellainen kauppareissu 
tällä kertaa! , Kommentoi alle mitä 
tykkäsit videosta, Ja tietysti paina ❤️ ja laita tili seurantaan

stickersText:
Millaista on käydä parturissa Bangkokissa ja mitä se maksaa? 💇‍♂️💈💸, Maailmanympärimatkalla🌏
Etappi 2
Maa Thaimaa
Kaupunki Bangkok, Juho meni Bmore Barbers BKK nimiseen parturiin tämä oli Google arvostelut 4,9/5, Tästä lähdettiin liikenteeseen, vähän jännittää kun ei ole tutussa parturintuolissa, Heti tuli hieman miinusta, kun parturi ei osannut juurikaan 🇬🇧. Onneksi löytyi puhelimesta vanha kuva edelliseltä parturikäynniltä, Paikan ulkonäöstä taas tuli plussaa. Mukavan rouheeta tyyliä, 🏀 ja 🛹teema oli vahvasti esillä, Suomen parhaat 💇🏼 on Helsingissä Otto’s Barber Shopin Otto, sekä Oulussa Salon Saran Ilpo, Oton kans tulee aina käytyä päivän polttavat puheenaiheet ja urheiluasiat läpi, Ilpolta saat parhaat ravintola -ja matkustusvinkit käytännössä minne tahansa onkaan menossa, Nämä miehet on äärimmäisen kovia ammattilaisia ja mahtavia ihmisiä!, Tähän parturikertaan en tällä kertaa ottanut hiustenpesua, Huomasi että kaveri on ennenkin leikannut hiuksia, Vähän meinasi väsyttääkkin, parturin tuolissa rentoutuu aina kummasti 😅, Laatu oli luokkaa MRoom tai GROOM, muttei lähellekkään Ilpon tai Oton tasoa, Parturikäynti maksoi 
500THB eli 13,47€, Paina ♥️ ja ota tili seurantaan, Millaista on käydä parturissa Bangkokissa ja mitä se maksaa?

Uskaltaisitko itse pitää mehiläiskennoa kädessä, kun se kuhisee mehiläisiä? 🐝, Maailmanympärimatkalla 
Etappi 2 🌏
Maa Vietnam
Kaupunki Ho Chi Minh City, Entä maistaa hunajaa suoraan kennosta, kun mehiläiset pörrää sun ympärillä?🐝, Tämä se vasta on tuoretta 🍯, Entäpä maistaisitko kobra käärmeestä tehtyä viinaa? 🐍, En määkään, onneksi sitä varten on semi yllytyshullu mies 😅, Maistui kuulemma saken ja viskin sekoitukselta, Mentiin siis tutustumaan Mekong-joen suistoalueeseem Etelä-Vietnamissa, Mekong-joki on yksi maailman pisimmästä ja sen pituuden takia myös mutaisimmista joista. Matkaa tänne oli autolla pari tuntia Ho Chi Minh Citystä., Mekong-joki on tärkeä paikallisille asukkaille, se  tarjoaa heille vettä, ravintoa, elinkeinon, vesivoimaa ja liikkumiskeinon. , Joki on kuitenkin ekokatastrofin partaalla sillä sitä uhkaa ilmastonmuutos, metsäkato, elinympäristöjen tuhoutuminen, patojen rakentaminen ja villieläinten laiton kauppa , Mekong joen suistoalue on myös yksi suosituimmista turistikohteista Vietnamissa, Vierailimme Mekong-joella Yksisarvissaarella, missä saatiin maistella paikallistuotannon herkkuja, Tarjolla oli mm. Kuivattua inkivääriä ja banaania, hunajateetä, hedelmiä ja kookoskarkkeja, Olipa mielenkiintoinen päivä! Yksi paras asia matkustamisessa on se että pääsee oppimaan paikallisesta kulttuurista, ihmisistä ja alueista , Paina 🧡 ja laita tili seurantaan!

desc: How I’ve traveled for 13 years 👇 (Save & share with someone who can relate!) Firstly, & honesty though I am very happy being single, especially after a painful breakup. I think it’s important to give yourself time to heal & work on fixing your own energy before taking on other peoples 🫶 Secondly, here’s HOW I’ve traveled so much: At 18 I went to Australia solo on a working holiday visa & worked for pretty much the whole time! Then visited some of Asia 🎉  During my university summers I went interrailling (thanks student overdraft) & worked a summer season in Greece as a waitress.  Post uni I worked 2 full time hour jobs (9-5 office & bar work evenings/ weekend), saved £3,500 & went away for 2.5 years.  I did this through budget backpacking, a working holiday visa in New Zealand for 2 years & volunteering for accom in Tonga & Hawaii.  Then I worked as a European Trip Leader for 2 years(thanks Covid)! I lead trips through a mix of 25 countries! I’d save during my trip leading seasons & use this money for personal travel in my months off between winter & summer. I also god discounts on Egypt & a trip around 6 African countries as I worked for a tour company! May 2021 I left the UK, started teaching English online, got a fully remote job & now I am a content creator, travel coach & social media strategist for brands.  I’ve also written an ebook which covers exactly how you can live this life too 🤩 So follow @daisystraveldiaries to learn how to travel full time & daily digital nomad tips! . . . #digitalnomadgirls #digitalnomad #fulltimetravel #solotravel #remoteworklife
hashtagNames: digitalnomadgirls, digitalnomad, fulltimetravel, solotravel, remoteworklife
stickersText: Don’t worry mum. I’m just doing a gap year while I’m 18 then I’ll settle down , Daisy did not settle down. Daisy is now 31 & has been traveling ever since. desc: The Future Workforce Alliance is proud to announce the first 3 signees of the European Charter for Digital Workplace Well-Being.  Lídia Pereira, Member of the European Parliament (EPP, PT) Dragos Pislaru, Member of the European Parliamnent (Renew, RO) Alex Agius Saliba, Member of the European Parliamnent (S&D, MT) This historic document aims to protect the mental health of remote & hybrid workers. We are deeply grateful to all 3 MEPs for their leadership and support. Now we are urging more MEPs to support the call for solutions that will improve the experience of remote working for current and future generations. desc: What started as a little escape from the hustle & bustle of General Luna in Siargao led to a love affair with the idyllic sanctuary of the north. Here are 4 reasons why you’ll fall for this enchanting paradise: 1- It has something magical & healing to it—the further north you go, the more you will see and feel it. Nature around here with oceanside roads are just captivating.  2- If you’re anything like me who embraces serene, local vibes, charming restaurants (yes, even with veggie options!), secluded beaches, and uncrowded surf breaks - the north is for you.  3- It’s a ‚everyone knows everyone kinda environment‘ so here you really have the chance to connect to a small, beautiful community. One thing that I just have to highlight is @kolekbibo, an NGO empowering local communities—check their beachfront restaurant, yoga and consider volunteering. 4- Amazing sunsets over the ocean (you don’t get that in the south!), whether you’re surfing into the golden hour or simply basking on the beach. 🤍 #TravelSiargao #SiargaoDiaries #Siargaoisland #siargao #Siargaovibes #SiargaoAdventures #filipino #filipinorelatable #filipinotiktok #Philippinesparadise #gophilippines #tropicalvibes #SurfingDestination #IslandLife #TravelInspiration #thatgirl #tropicalvibes #digitalnomadlife

desc: Quick introductions 😊 I’m Sarah, a digital nomad living in Buenos Aires, Argentina.  I’ve been here for 5+ years, and it’s been the absolute best experience of my life — follow along to learn why 👀    I met my now husband working at a ski resort in Colorado and, after falling in love in two short months, I moved to Argentina. (Yes, my friends & family thought I was nuts, but it worked out 😉)  Before moving to Argentina, I worked & traveled across several countries, so I have plenty of insight into living abroad.  And… I can now say without a shadow of a doubt: Buenos Aires is an INCREDIBLE place to be a digital nomad.  My hope is to inspire & empower other women who are interested in the digital nomad lifestyle with inside tips, resources, and reasons to start your journey in Buenos Aires. Because here’s the thing: you can absolutely do it! And you’re not alone. desc: After 6 years in my apartment everyday started to feel the same. New decorations didnt help. Saging wasn’t enough lol. I found new hobbies trying to make time pass. Then I finally asked God to guide me, point me in the direction that I needed to go. I’m the only child so it’s normal for me to stay in my bubble, and figure things out on my own. This time I was truly stuck. Then one day, I started reflect on these past few years. I made myself a priority, I started taking solo vacations, received a job in aviation, got more passport stamps, and last month I asked myself what’s truly stopping me from leaving? I never felt like I fit in with certain spaces, and now I realize I wasn’t supposed to. After researching for days, sacrificing sleep, selling all my material things, and reaching out to others that dare to be different… IM MOVING TO MEXICO! Follow me on this journey to find a apartment! Link in bio for my YouTube ✨ & thank you @Shawnie🧚🏾 @Jasx ✨ Bougie Hippie Abroad  @Creator • Coach • Expat @Lynette Adkins for sharing your experiences moving abroad & never looking back! desc: This might sound silly, but..  I was feeling restless and unproductive during my stay in General Luna in the south of Siargao. I sensed the need for a getaway, a place remote and serene, away from the hustle and bustle of the busy hub and social life. ✨ So, on a whim, I packed a small bag, strapped my surfboard onto my scooter, and headed north, all the way to the most northern point of Siargao Island. The 1.5-hour drive was filled with breathtaking scenery that only grew more beautiful as I ventured further. Along the way, I would pause, absorbing the incredible beauty that surrounded me, realizing that I was healing from something, anything. 🤍 When I arrived at my hotel, just a short walk from one of the most stunning, uncrowded beaches with crystal-clear waters, adorned by fishing boats and encircled by countless palm trees, I knew I had found my sanctuary. My days were spent either surfing alone, catching those perfect waves, or sharing the waves with just one other person. It was an incredible experience, feeling the power of the ocean and the freedom it brings. I dedicated time to building my website for @aryclub.official, finally ticking off substantial tasks while immersing myself in the beauty and tranquility of the surroundings. It goes without saying that I fell head over heels for the north of Siargao; there’s an undeniable magic in this area. The experience was a powerful reminder that sometimes, all it takes is a spontaneous journey to reconnect with ourselves and find solace in the beauty of nature. I feel a renewed sense of purpose and energy, ready to take on new challenges and continue the journey of reinventing myself. 🫶  If you’re ever in Siargao; you now know where to go 🦋 #SiargaoDiaries #surfergirl #digitalnomadlife  #surfinglife #reels #tropicalvibes #motivationalreel #inspirationalreel #healthandwellness #thatgirl #dailyhabit #Siargaoisland #siargao #Philippinesparadise #gophilippines #IslandLife #travelinspiration

desc: L’utilizzo delle sbarre può essere un ottimo modo per migliorare anche il tuo  livello di boxe! Richiedono una forte presa e un notevole sforzo della parte superiore del corpo, in particolare delle braccia, delle spalle e del dorso.  Questo tipo di allenamento può contribuire a sviluppare una maggiore forza nelle tue braccia e nei tuoi muscoli del torace, importanti per lanciare colpi potenti e per sostenere il tuo corpo durante i movimenti di difesa. Per eseguire correttamente gli esercizi alle sbarre, è necessario impegnare il core per mantenere l’equilibrio e la stabilità durante i movimenti. Questo aiuterà a rafforzare i muscoli addominali e della schiena, fornendo una base solida per i tuoi movimenti quando ti muovi in guardia da boxe. Per allenare le gambe, concentrati sugli Squat jump che essendo un esercizio Pliometrico, contribuirà a sviluppare una maggiore potenza nelle gambe, che potrai sfruttare durante le combinazioni di colpi e i movimenti esplosivi sul ring. L’attrezzatura che ti serve è semplice e la puoi trovare: in palestra, al parchetto o anche a casa (con un piccolo investimento)! No scuse! stickersText: Why is Portugal overrated? 🇵🇹, I've been living in Portugal for a year and a half, and let me tell you, the hype you see in Times Square doesn't match the reality, 1️⃣ Crazy high cost of living! If you want to do business, get ready to fork over a ton , 3️⃣ Conservative society not ready for change or immigrants. desc: How to find remote work 👇 (SAVE for your job hunt!) I’ve had THE BEST summer in Europe! I spent time in Malta, Ibiza & then spent 7 nights Sailing around Croatia! My heart feels so full from all the amazing people I met, the cold Aperol I drank & the opportunities I got through social media which I never would’ve dreamt were possible this time last year (thank you ALL OF YOU for following and being part of this community, you’re changing my life & I hope I am helping you to change your’s & live this life too!) In a couple of weeks, I’m heading to Bali, Thailand then Sri Lanka & Nepal to host group trips! If you guys want to join me then send me a DM for info! If you want to live this full-time travel, digital nomad life then I’m here to help & cheer you on every step of the way bebeh! No matter what age 🎉 It took a LONG TIME to figure this out and made many mistakes along the way but now I’m sharing it all with you! First up: you could get a remote job! To find one, try these websites: * angel.co * remote.co * remotewomen.com * inkedin.com/jobs * workingnomads.com * nodesk.co * weworkremotely.com * FlexJobs * Fiverr * Upwork  If you want to travel long term but don’t fancy a laptop job then you could try:  1/ Working holiday visas: allow you to live & work in certain countries such as Australia & NZ for up to 2 years.  2/ Seasonal Work: Companies hire people in various roles to go & work a winter or summer season at their resort/ hotel/ camp. Usually, you get flights, accommodation, food & pay! 3/ Work for Accommodation: volunteer at a place in exchange for free accom. OR, you can collaborate & create content for places, again in exchange for free accom (you can charge for this sometimes too) 4/ Trip leader: Tour companies hire you to lead the trip. So you go on trips around whichever country/ city etc.  I go over all these details in my ebook: 6 Ways to Work & Travel the World, which is currently 50% off, only $15 :) Follow @daisystraveldiaries for daily tips on how to travel solo as a digital nomad 🥰 . . . #travel #digitalnomad #digitalnomads #digitalnomadlifestyle #fulltimetravel #travelfulltime #workandtravel #remotework #remoteworking

desc: I swam aboard a sexy man’s boat this day, for real 👀👇 (Save & share with someone who’d do this) What really happened in this video: a group of friends and I went out on a boat in Ibiza where we drank rose, danced, swam & lived our best lives. As you can see I just love to dance & groove so was in the zone then my friends drone scared the EFF out of me. But carried on anyway… I also love my friends in the background joining in the groove 🤣 On this day I also hijacked a neighbouring boat 😂. I saw a sailing boat close to ours with some beautiful men on board & it looked like they lived in it so I wanted to know their story… I jumped into the water with my bucket hat on, swam over and started chatting to them. They gave me a beer and let me have a look on the boat (it was close to our boat though & i made sure I was in sight of my friends at all times as safety first). I then jumped off the bow & swam back to my friends… it felt like a true mamma mia moment 😆 Turns out the owner is an Italian guy who lets people live on his boat all summer to help him out sailing around the Med. Then in the winter he worked for theatre companies!  Sooo cool. This is my fav part of traveling, hearing other people’s stories in the world 🌸 What’s your fav travel story you’ve learnt from a stranger? 🎉 Follow @daisystraveldiaries for daily travel & digital nomad tips 🌸 . . . #digitalnomadlifestyle #digitalnomadgirl #travel #solotravel #remoteworking #ibiza

Seeing the aftermath of the storm was shocking, especially seeing the lamposts that were snapped in half! Super grateful that we were inside the whole time!  #digitalnomad #digitalnomadlifestyle #biketouring #biketour #serbia #storm

stickersText:
Miten 🇯🇵 ruokakauppa 
eroaa 🇫🇮?, Maailmanympärimatkalla 🌏
Etappi 2
Maa Japani
Kaupunki Tokio, Ja mitä erikoisuuksia siellä tuli vastaan?, Ihan ensiksi heti ruokakaupan ovella oli sateenvarjoille teline, niitä ei suositeltu viedä kauppaan, Sekä sisäänkäynti sen verran kapee et piti pakittaa sisään, koska joku pakkas ostoksia vähän leveämmällä linjalla 😅, Heviosasto oli aika vaatimaton, mutta perus elintarvikkeet 🍎🥒🫑🍌🥬 löytyi , 🥒pussi 1,28€
🫑pussi 0,99€
🍎pussi 3,29€
🧅pussi 1,28€
🍌pussi 1,47€
🍅rasia 2,57€, Tuorelihaosasto oli todella suppea, 0,5kg paketti porsaanlihasuikaleita 2,95€, Melkeinpä kaikki liha oli esivalmistettua ja se oli pitkälti 🐷, Hieman oli hankala löytää mitä ruokaa on missäkin paketissa, sillä juuri missään ei lukenut englanniksi ja 🇯🇵 kirjaimet ei ole meille kovin tuttuja , Onneksi kananmunan ja tofun tunnisti ilman isompia tulkintoja, Tofua myytiin todella paljon ja vaikka miten erilailla maustettuna , Juho löysi olutnakkeja ja ehdotti sitä sekä🍺 ruoaksi, mutta Jenna ei ihan lämmennyt 😅, Täällä kaikki meidän näkemät ruokakaupat on luokkaa Alepa. Osaako joku sanoa onko Tokiossa Cittarin kokoisia kauppoja?, Kuivattua katkarapuja, Täällä on todella paljon kuivattua ruokaa, joka sitten keittäessä saa kuulemma normaalit mittasuhteet ja maun, Kuivattua ruohosipulia, Kuivattua merilevänsuikaleita, Kuivattua mangoa, Täälläkin ☕️ on pikakahvia 😡, Valmiiksi keitetty riisiä oli useampi paketti huoneenlämpöisessä hyllyssä , 0,63€/pkt, Valmiiksi leikattua 🥒 oli myös muutama eri rasia , Molemmat n. 0,8€/pkt, Täällä ei ruokakaupoissa ole kovin paljoa karkkeja, mutta valmiita jälkiruokia senkin edestä, Ja Jennan piti tottakai saada testata paikallisia sipsejä 😅, Ja samalla yllätettiin Juho haahuilemasta noodelihyllyllä 😂, Jogurttihyllystä löytyi kaikki tarpeellinen , 4-pack biojogurttia 1,22€, Teetä löytyi kylmänä laaja valikoima, 🥖🍞hyllyn valikoima oli todella suppea ja esim täysjyväleivästä sai monesti vain haaveilla, 🍺 ja muita mietoja alkoholituotteita oli myytävänä kohtuu laaja valikoima, mutta monipakkauksia ei juurikaan ollut, 6-pack oli isoin, 6-pack 0,5l tölkkejä n. 4,5€, Zero Cola Jack Daniels mixeri 1,28€/tlk, Kupillinen Sakea oli 1,34€, Täällä oli onneksi hyvä valikoima soodavesiä 😊, 1,25l plo 0,57€, Täällä kaupassa myydään myös väkeviä alkoholituotteita. Milloinhan me saadaan 🇫🇮 viinit kauppoihin? 🤔, Täällä myydään valtaosa ruoasta tosiaan esivalmistettuna tai kokonaan valmiina aterioina, joko kuivattuna tai pakastettuna, 🍦🍨hyllyn valikoima oli laaja, Eineshyllystä löytyi tottakai keitettyä riisiä. 🇯🇵 kuulemma tämmöinen keitetty riisipala on sama asia kuin meillä leipäpala, Tämä nakkinoodeliwokki vaikutti aika eksoottiselta 😅, Sitten kassalle, Paikalliset kassahihnat oli vähän lyhyen oloisia, Tupakkatuotteet saa olla 🇯🇵 edelleen näkyvillä , Maksukortti toimii joka ruokakaupassa, missä ollaan käyty, Kuitti annetaan aina kahdella kädellä ja pienesti kumarretaan asiakkaalle, Mitähän etikettimokia tässä meillä on tullut kauppareissulla tehtyä? 😅, Paina ♥️ ja pistä tili seurantaan!, Japanilainen vs suomalainen ruokakauppa

desc: I started my Etsy shop in March/April 2022. I was due with my second baby, coming in early May, and my goal was to have my Etsy shop up before I gave birth.  I figured to get sales; I would have to promote my shop on social media. So I set it up, planning to return to it a few months post-baby.  May baby was born. I got zero sales.  June, I wasn’t paying attention, but I got a few organic sales.  July, I realized I was getting a few sales here and there. I think I made $158 that month.  August, I dove back into it, hoping to make an extra $500 a month passively from my shop. I tweaked my product, bringing me to my first $1k. This video explains the strategy that I used: @Des | Selling Digital Products  In the last year, my shop has made over $45k in revenue. All from products I made essentially one time (with minor tweaks here and there), and I have never had to promote my shop 🤯 Here is what I wish I had known when I had started:@Des | Selling Digital Products  #figuringitoutonline #sellingcanvatemplates #workfromanywhere #etsypassiveincome #sellingonetsy #

desc: Why I ended up alone in a coconut boat 👇 (Save & save for your trip!) 📍Hoi An, Vietnam. Coconut boats  I visited Vietnam solo recently & was staying in hotels or private rooms as I’m a digital nomad so work in the day or evenings / I just don’t do dorms any more darlings 🙏 So I signed up to this coconut boat trip & cooking class (oioi Miss Gordon Ramsey) as I thought it would be more fun to do the boats with people 🫶 When we got there I realised it was two to a boat but everyone else was already signed up in a pair so I was alone. I go early didn’t mind though but I think the people felt bad for me … yeah gimmie sympathy you loved up betches.  BUT, after about 10 minutes, my boat man & I started to try and communicate then just started constantly laughing at each other for the next 20 minutes 🤣🤣 he then kept telling me g his mates something in Vietnamese and they kept laughing at me too. I was sweating and crying with the amount of laughter.  We had no idea what the other person was saying but OMG we laughed.  The cooking class was then as a big group so met some really cool people! 😊🥂 So this is your sign to book that ticket, talk with the locals and just HAVE FUN!  Or, book into my group trip in Nepal next month or Thailand in March to travel with a group of like minded legends with all the laughs 😂 Follow @daisystraveldiaries for daily travel & digital nomad tips!  . . . #digitalnomad #solotravel #locationindependent #travelgirlsgo #digitalnomadgirls

stickersText:
Biggest observations I’ve made as a Brit 🇬🇧 living in Rio de Janeiro 🇧🇷, So far…, 1. Climate , Obvious one I know, Sig. hotter all year round, Anything lower than 15 degrees is regarded as ‘cold’ 😳, Seasons are inverted so we’re about to enter summer, Seasons are inverted so we’re about to enter summer, Which makes seeing Xmas decorations very strange 🥴, Which makes seeing Xmas decorations very strange 🥴, 2. Events, I lived in Cardiff and Manchester before moving here , But the amount of things to do and see here is on another level, Any day
Any time
Any budget 
Any interest , The best bit is you don’t get FOMO for missing an event because there’ll be something even bigger one tomorrow , 3. Work/life balance , So much more of a relaxed culture, * I can only talk for Rio and am not generalising about a whole population , I’ve been here 7 weeks and there’s already been 4 bank holidays , The best way I’ve heard it described is 

“People in Europe and US live to work and people here work to live” , 4. Natural Scenery, Absolutely unbelievable., Quite easily some of the best views and settings I’ve ever seen, It manages to have…

Mountains, World famous beaches, Rainforests! , And incredible viewpoints, Within 30 minutes of a giant metropolis!

desc: My favorite activity in Oaxaca! Details below 👇🏼 This waterfall is Cascada de Santiago Apoala and you can visit it as part of a tour if you’re staying at @Co404coliving in Oaxaca. The tour was 850 pesos (~$50 USD) and included a guide and transportation to and from the waterfall. It was 12 hours in total, so a bit of a long day, but definitely worth it! Most people who go to Oaxaca prioritize visiting Hierve el Agua, but from what I’ve heard, that spot is a lot more touristy and less of an adventure than Apoala. If you have time, maybe try to visit both, otherwise, you can’t go wrong with this one. I really enjoyed my stay at Co404 too! It was nice having so many activities to choose from and I love the emphasis they put on fostering a community of digital nomads in Oaxaca. They also have a location in San Cristóbal… If I had more time, I’d love to check out that one as well. 👀 Let me know if you have any questions! desc: 🌏👣 La ricerca della libertà  🌴💻 Qualche tempo fa ho avuto la fortuna di conoscere Gianluca Gotto @gianluca.gotto di persona e scambiarci qualche chiacchera. Eravamo a Bali, e grazie ad una grande idea di @stefaniadips , che non smetterò mai di ringraziare, abbiamo girato una breve chiaccherata/intervista. Gianluca ha condiviso con me il suo percorso: dal desiderio ardente di libertà e autonomia nel gestire il proprio tempo, fino alla decisione di abbandonare l’Italia a 20 anni per esplorare opportunità in Australia. La svolta è arrivata nel 2013 a Vancouver, dove si è posto una domanda cruciale: “Come posso vivere secondo le mie regole?” 🌍✨ La risposta? Trasformare la scrittura in un ponte verso la libertà. Da quel momento, Gianluca ha abbracciato a pieno la vita da Nomade Digitale, trovando nell’indipendenza e nella flessibilità del lavoro remoto la realizzazione del suo desiderio di libertà. Questa conversazione è stata un vero tocco di ispirazione per me. Mi ha ricordato quanto possa essere potente e trasformativa la scelta di una vita meno convenzionale, guidata dalla libertà e dall’autonomia. 🌟 E tu, hai mai sognato di cambiare vita e diventare nomadi digitali? Quali sono i tuoi desideri di libertà e come li persegui? desc: It’ll never feel real - and it’ll never last. I was talking to my brother @joewhisney recently and we caught up talking about funny family things and how stoked dad would be about where we are in life. Me - “Yeah, I’m incredibly lucky to be able to live the life I’m living right now.” Joe - “I wouldn’t say it’s luck, you worked for it.” The truth is - we both did. Very little luck was involved. He’s an incredibly talented high-level trainer, and I travel Sure, dad would be excited where we both are physically. But he’d be much more proud of the men we’ve become. We also talked about how different life has become the past two years. Things are, like, vastly different. “God, that feels like a lifetime ago,” Joe said when we were reminded of the roadtrip we took to drop him off at Arizona State. “It sort of was, huh,” I said alluding to how fucking different life is now. Holidays are different. Relationships are different. Heck, simple conversations are different. —————— We have current stories of mom and her quirks, mom’s relatives and their quirks, stories of our own - but no more of dad. Just words and phrases that yank us right back to a time when he would say them. I don’t know why all of these videos are making me miss my dad so much, but they’re proving to be a great way to help me grieve.  Enough rambling. Thanks for reading. 🌹 🌹 🌹 #digitalnomad #digitalnomadlife #roadtrip #griefjourney #grief #griefandloss

desc: As a dog owner, you become familiar with the idea of a “soul dog”. A dog that feels like an extension of yourself or a dog that makes you feel whole - one you’ll never forget. My soul dog was Tank. I still get deeply sad when I think about him. All of the things he was there for and all of his quirks. The whispery bark he had towards the end of his life, the relationship my roommates had with him, our last few months together. They are all things that have become a thin, distant memory. Plus, I’ve got Pepper now. From the day my dad brought Pepper home I jokingly insisted that she would be mine someday. Little did I know the circumstances under which I would adopt her were much darker than I had originally hoped but hey - life, ya know? For the past almost two years, she’s been the last thing that I think about when I go to sleep and the first thing that I think about when I wake up. Both largely due to her sleeping positions. And, well, because I love her so damn much. She’s one of the biggest reasons we’ve embarked on this phase of life. So I can give her the life my dad never really wanted. See, he loved the idea of having a dog but didn’t love to do the dog owner things. Walks, socializing, nothing. He just wanted a companion - and I can completely understand that. So now she’s my companion as we continue to look for the next best trail. And, damnit, I’m going to fill up my phone with videos of her wiggly but and wirey tail. I can have two soul dogs, right? Come on who said only one!? #silverlab #silverlabrador #digitalnomad #digitalnomadlifestyle #hike #hiking

desc: Another popular travel destination is adding a digital nomad visa! 🇯🇵🏯  According to the Japan Times, the Japanese government has tentatively set a launch date of March 2024 to roll out a six-month visa for digital nomads. Visa Qualifications * They must make a minimum of ¥10 million per year (roughly USD$68,341 based on current conversion rates). * They must have private international health coverage, not Japan’s. * People who are self-employed or considered independent contractors must show proof of work and documentation.  * Spouses and children will be allowed to live in Japan with the visa holder. They must be covered by private international insurance as well. * The visa will be offered to visitors from 49 countries and territories, including the United States, Australia, and more. How to get the visa from Japan 🇯🇵 We’re still waiting on new details since there’s no concrete details. Like normal visa processes, interested applicants will most likely need necessary documents and evidence of their employment and apply at a local Japanese embassy. Afar says, “We can expect more specifics to emerge in the coming weeks as the program gets closer to its official launch date this March.” #liveandworkinjapan #digitalnomadlifestyle #japanvisa #travelnews #traveltok #japantiktok #japantravel #remotework

desc: Things to Know before you move to Playa Del Carmen Mexico or if you’re thinking about coming as a digital nomad:  1. It’s loud 😅 if you value a good night’s sleep bring ear plugs  2. It’s not as affordable as other parts of Mexico unless you are in a very local area 3. No Uber but you you can use Radio Taxi to order a ride through their app or whatsapp number  4. Playa is walkable and most places you can also reach by bike 5. There’s a really nice grocery store here called Chedraui with everything you need. There’s also Walmart and Sams  6. There’s a good amount of expats here especially in the Playacar area  7. Join local expat facebook groups to network for things you may need 8. There’s alot of police everywhere so be prepared for that but over all we have felt safe walking around  9. There’s alot of construction happening so it is also loud during the day  10. The beaches are beautiful but they do get seaweed during certain times of the year and it can smell pretty bad. desc: How to travel full time👇  (Save this for your journey) P.s. I’m hosting a group trip in Thailand from March 27th - April 4th to connect people who want to live this life & to teach you how from paradise 🤩🤩 I moved to Australia solo on a working holiday visa & since then haven’t really stopped! I studied Psychology at University but would travel in my uni holidays & then left the UK for 2.5years after uni & the rest is history.  I am now a full time travel content creator but I only became this at the age of 30 (it’s never too late to change your carer 😂). Before making money through social media though I used other methods to travel full time.  These are the ways I have managed to travel full time: First up: you could get a remote job! To find one, try these websites: * angel.co * remote.co * remotewomen.com * inkedin.com/jobs * workingnomads.com * nodesk.co * weworkremotely.com * FlexJobs * Fiverr * Upwork  Ways I have traveled full time whilst NOT working online: 1/ Working holiday visas: allow you to live & work in certain countries such as Australia & NZ for up to 2 years. I did this at 18 in Oz then 22 in NZ.  2/ Seasonal Work: Companies hire people in various roles to go & work a winter or summer season at their resort/ hotel/ camp. Usually, you get flights, accommodation, food & pay! I did this in Greece & was the worlds worse waitress & pretty much got fired 🙃 3/ Work for Accommodation: volunteer at a place in exchange for free accom. OR, you can collaborate & create content for places, again in exchange for free accom (you can charge for this sometimes too)! I did this in Costa Rica, Tonga, Hawaii & more.  4/ Trip leader: Tour companies hire you to lead the trip. So you go on trips around whichever country/ city etc. I did this for two years around Europe with @topdecktravel  5/ Teach English Online: my fav platform for this was @italki but I’ve also heard good things about @preply  Follow @daisystraveldiaries for daily tips on how to travel solo as a digital nomad 🥰 . . . #travel #digitalnomad #digitalnomads #digitalnomadlifestyle #fulltimetravel #travelfulltime #workandtravel #remotework #remoteworking

desc: This post is bery vulnerable for me. Long story short - my job was unsupportive of me being a pregnant military spouse and having to live overseas, despite no legal or tax implications to the employer due to me having a special visa allowing me to be a US based employee while working remotely from Italy. Thid was a difficult situation for me because I liked my job and it pained me to have to have to make this choice. ##terminated##quit##HR##jobs##work##wfh##workfromhome##remotework##military##militarywife##vulnerable##sahm##fyp
hashtagNames: terminated, quit, hr, jobs, work, wfh, workfromhome, remotework, military, militarywife, vulnerable, sahm, fyp
stickersText:
POV you’re being fired because you’re a military spouse with legal rights to work overseas remotely but your HR could care less., I showed them the agreement between the Italian and US government permitting military spouses to work overseas under US employment law but it didn’t matter., I took this matter very seriously. I enjoyed my job and it paid well. I had good performance reviews and was not prepared to leave., I wanted my boss to know how much I appreciated her hiring me., Getting chocked up because I genuinely do like my job and have been working it remotely in Italy with no issues for the past month., Family always comes first , It was hard for me to keep it together. I’m also pregnant so the pregnancy hormones don’t help 😩, I asked for more time (even just a few days) to wrap up my work projects., Without acknowledging how difficult this is for me, the response was an immediate “no” and let me know today would be my last day., My boss was on the call with HR. It was the first time she spoke. She also showed no compassion., HR requested I return to the states (with no health insurance) or quit., All they cared about was getting their equipment back. There was 0 empathy for my situation., Just a reminder that you are always replaceable at work but irreplaceable to your family. ,      POV  you’re
being   terminated     from   your   job

desc: Ever been ambushed by cuteness? Imagine wandering the streets of Romania, where the cat distribution system is, let's say, purrfectly unconventional. Here, the night doesn't just belong to revelers and the echoes of history; it's also the prime time for feline forces to mobilize. You're never just walking alone; you're on a potential adoption spree, guided by the stealthy paws of the night's furriest inhabitants. These aren't your average, well-groomed house cats waiting to be Instagram stars. No, these are the rugged, the survivors, the whiskered wanderers with tales (and tails) that could rival any seasoned traveler. They're the kind of cats that don't just meow; they communicate in a dialect of purrs, hisses, and soulful gazes that say, "You. Yes, you. You're my human now." The cat population here doesn't need an invitation. They've got the run of the place, turning the narrow alleys, ancient ruins, and even modern cityscapes into their personal playgrounds. But what's truly fascinating is how these feline denizens embody the spirit of adventure and resilience. They're not just surviving; they're thriving, in a country that's as complex and layered as the history it's built upon. They invite you, the unsuspecting traveler, to pause, to stoop down for a closer look, and perhaps, to find a companion you didn't know you were looking for. So, the next time you're navigating the mysteries of Romania, ask yourself: Are you really ready for the cat-venture of a lifetime? desc: Tag a friend and say nothing🤓 Ever had a roommate who moos? In the lush landscapes of Romania, amidst its rolling hills and vibrant green pastures, the idea of keeping a cow as a pet isn't as far-fetched as one might think. This country known for its rich traditions and deep-rooted connection with nature, offers a unique perspective on animal companionship. Here, animals are not just part of the landscape; they're part of the family. In Romania, agriculture plays a crucial role, with over 3.8 million households engaged in farming activities, a testament to the country's agrarian lifestyle. Among these, the cow holds a special place, often seen as a member of the family rather than just livestock. It's not uncommon to find cows being treated with the same affection and care reserved for household pets in urban areas. They roam freely in the countryside, contributing significantly to the rural economy through dairy and beef production, and in some cases, even becoming beloved pets. But would you let one bunk with you? While the idea of sharing your bed with a bovine friend might seem outlandish, it symbolizes a deeper connection between humans and animals in Romanian culture. This bond transcends the conventional, embracing a holistic view of living harmoniously with nature. It begs the question: In a world where pets often become our closest companions, how do we define the limits of this relationship? Could a cow, with its gentle eyes and serene demeanor, become not just a pet but a part of the family? What's your take on unconventional pets shaping our lives and homes? desc: Note to self: if you have a drone in your camera kit, don’t leave the airport during a long layover in Cairo.  We know the law on drones in Egypt, but with a 17 hour layover after a crazy few days of travel we didn’t even think of it when we found out there was a hotel connected to our terminal. When heading to catch out flight we ran into a *slight* problem when asked if there was a drone in our bag. We’ll keep it at that for now because obviously the drone is in our possession, and all of us caught our connecting flight, but it was definitely a firm reminder to check and REMEMBER every country’s laws on drone usage and possession even if you’re only heading to the airport hotel to sleep 💤 .  If you ever fly in Zanzibar, just know that every child in the village will run out to where you’re flying. Kojo flew for the kids for what seemed like hours this night until it started getting too dark out.  #familytravel #houstonfamily #houstonblogger #multiculturalfamily #multiculturalcouple #travellife #africatravel #zanzibar

How to apply for the Spanish Digital Nomad Visa (DNV), You need to have a valid TIE if you wanna do the modificación, For PH companies:
BIR
DTI
Mayor’s permit
All apostilled and translated , US companies: 
Certificate of good standing
Apostilled & translated, Letter from your company/client stating that you’re  allowed to work from Spain, Police background check from your country 
(NBI for the PH) 
Apostilled & translated , Invoices and at least 3 months worth of bank statements showing your salary, €2,650 or 168k php, It took exactly 20 working days, They asked for the “AEAT”, I filed the declaración de la renta for 2022 & 2023, You don’t have to be married to apply together!!, We submitted the justificante of our PDH application , DNV’s approved here are valid for 3 years vs 1 year from outside Spain

desc: “How has it been living in London as a digital nomad for the past 3 months?” An EXPERIENCE. This has been such a life changing experience, so much so that I pushed my flight date back 2 months and I’m now leaving in September instead of July 😂 — the whole reason I moved to London was because I regretted not studying abroad as a student and I  now feel like I truly have an idea of what living in another country feels like which I’ve always longed for.  It’s challenging, but breeds growth, open-mindedness, community, and new perspective on both the US and the UK. Can’t wait to share even more about this experience as I have sooo many thoughts! If you’re considering doing something like this for even a month, I’d say DO IT. These past 3 months have far exceeded anything I could’ve imagined and reading about other countries and cultures in textbooks or the news is so different than actually living somewhere, experiencing it’s laws, people, social norms, shortcomings, and strengths in real-time. I’m incredibly grateful 🩵

desc: Here are 28 great questions to ask in a job interview  @Anna Papalia  Questions about the specific job 1.     What are your expectations for me in this role? 2.    What’s the most important thing I should accomplish in the first 90 days (https://hbr.org/books/watkins)? 3.    What’s the performance review process like here? How often would I be formally reviewed? 4.    What metrics or goals will my performance be evaluated against? 5.    What are the most immediate projects that I would take on? 6.    How long before I will be… [meeting with clients, have responsibility for my own accounts, interacting with other departments, etc.]? Questions about the team 7.    What types of skills is the team missing that you’re looking to fill with a new hire? 8.   What are the biggest challenges that I might face in this position? 9.    Do you expect my main responsibilities in this position to change in the next six months to a year? 10.Can you tell me about the team I’ll be working with? 11.  Who will I work with most closely? What other departments or units will I interact with? 12. Can you tell me about my direct reports? What are their strengths and the team’s biggest challenges? Questions for your potential boss 13. How long have you been at the company? 14. How long have you been a manager? 15. What’s your favorite part of working here? Questions about the company  16. What are the current goals that the company is focused on, and how does this team work to support hitting those goals? 17. What gets you most excited about the company’s future? 18.How would you describe the company’s values? 19. How has the company changed over the last few years? 20.                 What are the company’s plans for growth and development? Questions about the culture 21. How do you typically onboard employees?  o   If the position will be remote, ask specifically about how remote employees are integrated into the company culture, Markman advises. 22.                  What do new employees typically find surprising after they start? 23.                  Is there anything that I should read before starting that would help me have a shared understanding with my colleagues?  o   Asking this question not only signals your interest in the position but also shows that you’re eager to have “shared cultural references with the people you’ll be working with,” Markman says. 24.                  What’s your favorite office tradition? 25.                  What do you and the team usually do for lunch? 26.                  Do you ever do joint events with other departments or teams? 27.What’s different about working here than anywhere else you’ve worked? 28.                  How has the co mpany changed since you joined? #jobinterview #interviewprep #interviewtips #questionstoask #howtointerview

desc: Craving an escape into a landscape that feels almost otherworldly? In the heart of Transylvania, there’s a hidden haven where nature’s splendor is on full display. Imagine standing amidst the towering Carpathian Mountains, their rugged peaks often kissed by clouds, offering a majestic and serene backdrop. This isn’t just scenery; it’s an immersive experience where every vista tells a story of timeless beauty and tranquility. Transylvania’s rolling hills and expansive valleys are a feast for the eyes. In spring and summer, the meadows burst into vibrant colors, blanketed with wildflowers that sway gently in the breeze. The forests here are ancient, filled with towering trees and crisscrossed by crystal-clear streams that sparkle in the sunlight. Each trail you take unveils new panoramas – from sun-dappled clearings to sweeping views that stretch across miles of untouched wilderness. The air is filled with the fresh scent of pine and earth, and the silence is profound, broken only by the rustle of leaves and the distant murmur of streams. As you explore, you’ll encounter some of the most breathtaking lookout points. Imagine the sense of awe as you stand on a secluded plateau, gazing out over a sea of green that seems to go on forever, framed by the dramatic silhouettes of the Carpathian peaks. Whether you’re hiking along scenic trails, resting by a mountain stream, or simply soaking in the panoramic vistas from a quiet hilltop, every moment here is a reminder of nature’s raw and untouched beauty. How does this place make you feel about the simple, unadulterated wonders of the world? desc: Could you do it? 90 years old and still making the youngsters look like amateurs. In a tucked-away corner of Romania, where time seemed to have frozen in a poignant dance with tradition, I stumbled upon a living testament to the indomitable spirit of life. A grandma, a matriarch in the heart of her village, carving poetry with a scythe in her “batatura,” the courtyard that cradled generations of stories. This wasn’t just about cutting grass; it was an ode to survival etched in every swing of the weathered scythe. An elderly woman, a silhouette against the backdrop of rolling hills and rustic charm, maneuvering a tool almost as ancient as her. The rhythmic cadence of the blade carving through the grass sang a ballad of resilience that transcended the boundaries of time. It was as if the scythe itself held the secrets of a thousand lifetimes, whispered through the hands of those who had faced hardship head-on. In the heart of Romanian villages, where the air is heavy with the tales of survival and shared history, the elders cultivate more than just crops. Our grandma, with her face etched in lines of laughter and wisdom, was a guardian of a fading dialect – the language of resilience, of grit. The scythe, a silent protagonist in this tale, became a bridge connecting the elderly to the present, a tool passed down like an heirloom, carrying the weight of memories in its worn blade.  As she honed that blade with a special stone and cleaned it with freshly cut grass, it wasn’t just about maintaining a tool; it was a ritual, a communion with a way of life that had weathered storms and stood resilient against the test of time. desc: Guys, aku sering banget denger orang pengen kerja remote tapi nggak tau harus mulai dari mana. Atau bahkan udah coba tapi masih belum berhasil. Nih, aku kasih beberapa alasan umum yang sering aku temuin: Mindset "Aku Nggak Bisa" Banyak yang merasa skill mereka nggak cukup. Padahal, kadang yang kurang itu bukan skill, tapi kepercayaan diri. Nggak Tau Mau Mulai Dari Mana Bingung platform mana yang cocok, atau skill apa yang perlu dipelajari. Overwhelmed sama banyaknya info di luar sana. Takut Kompetisi Mikir kalo dunia kerja remote itu udah penuh dan susah masuknya. Trust me, masih banyak peluang kok! Comfort Zone Udah nyaman sama kerjaan sekarang, takut ambil risiko. Padahal, growth happens outside your comfort zone. Kurang Konsisten Udah mulai apply tapi baru beberapa kali langsung nyerah. Padahal, konsistensi itu kunci. Skill Belum Update Masih pake skill lama yang mungkin udah kurang relevan di pasar kerja remote. Personal Branding Kurang Kuat Belum bisa 'jualan diri' dengan baik di platform kerja remote. Belum Dapet Kerja Udah apply sana-sini tapi belum ada yang nerima. Jangan patah semangat! Mungkin perlu evaluasi lagi strategi apply kamu. Nah, gimana? Ada yang merasa familiar sama alasan-alasan di atas? Inget ya, semua hambatan itu bisa diatasi kok. Yang penting, kamu mau mulai dan konsisten. Pengen tau cara ngatasin hambatan-hambatan ini? Follow terus akun ini, karena aku bakal sharing tips dan trik buat sukses di dunia kerja remote. Yuk, share di komen, apa sih yang bikin kamu belum mulai kerja remote sampai sekarang? --- Halo, aku Agni Raraswulan. Aku udah pernah kerja remote buat perusahaan di Asia, Eropa, sama Amerika. Pengalaman aku sebagai Operations Manager, aku ngerekrut dan ngatur talent remote dari banyak negara. Aku mau berbagi info soal kerja remote yang bisa bantu kamu dapetin kerjaan di perusahaan luar negeri. Ikutin akun ini buat dapetin info seputar dunia kerja remote ya! Pengen tau lebih banyak atau ada yang mau ditanyain? aku mau banget ngobrol bareng kalian di GRUP KOMUNITAS, udah ada di profile. GRATIS KOK>_< #kerjadarimanasaja #remoteworker #workfromanywhere #digitalnomad #belajarkerjaremotebarengagni

desc: Avoid the crowds at Maya Bay! Everyone wants that special photo or video of THAT beach from The Beach, otherwise known as Maya Bay.  It’s one of the most popular beaches in Thailand and there are thousands of visitors to it every day. There are tours from Krabi and Phuket but you want to AVOID those. Instead get a ferry to Phi Phi (we stayed for one night) and then get the early bird ‘Maya Bay Avoid The Crowds’ tour with @GetYourGuide . It’s an early start (meet at 6am by the pier) but you will see the sunrise over the water and get to Maya Bay by 7am when it opens to tourists.  There will still be a large group of you but if you head to the viewpoint first, you will get your photos and videos of the beach with no one on it.  My children were also the only kids on this beach when we were there too. Incredible. A beautiful place. 🩷 #thebeach #travelthailand #mayabay #digitalnomadlife #travellingwithkids #travelwithkids #thailand #phiphiislands #getyourguide #mayabaybeach
