desc: Grateful is an understatement 🙏🏼 Six months ago I made the decision to close my chapter of living in LA and embark on the adventure of digital nomad life, something I’ve always dreamed of.  I remember sitting on my couch in April 2024, alone on a Friday night, thinking, “I am not living life to the fullest.”  I’ve been in the unique position of being able to work from anywhere, single, no kids, and absolutely nothing tying me to living in one place. Traveling the world is a dream of mine so I realized if I’m going to do it, the time is now.  I’m also in my mid-30s, and proving that this is something you can do at any age, not just in your 20s! A new friend of mine from London is 40 and doing the same thing 🙃 Starting the new year in Bali is something I’m beyond grateful to be doing. See the legendary yellow Tram 28 🚋 – This tram is a true symbol of Lisbon, winding through the city’s most picturesque neighborhoods. 4. Walk along the Tejo River waterfront 🌊 – Unwind with the sea breeze and snap some photos with a view of the 25th of April Bridge. 5. Recharge with a Portuguese espresso (Bica) ☕ – Extra energy is always a good idea, especially during Web Summit! 6. Visit Time Out Market 🍴 – Take a break at this popular food court featuring Lisbon’s best dishes, from tapas to seafood, all crafted by local chefs. 7. Catch the sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte 🌅 – This spot offers stunning views of Lisbon, especially at golden hour. desc: Aku baru-baru ini baca data yang bikin aku terkesan sekaligus prihatin. Ternyata, 7,5% PDB Filipina itu berasal dari kerja remote! Remote working juga jadi penggerak ekonomi di daerah-daerah terpencil India. Kenapa bisa gitu? Ternyata, di negara mereka sendiri, lapangan kerjanya terbatas. Jadi mereka harus cari kerja remote untuk negara lain, kebanyakan negara maju. Nah, kalau dipikir-pikir, kondisi ini nggak jauh beda sama di Indonesia. Berapa banyak pengangguran di negara kita? Jakarta makin sesak karena pusat lapangan kerja ada di sana. Padahal, remote working bisa jadi solusi untuk ngurangin pengangguran di Indonesia dan gerakin ekonomi di daerah, tanpa harus pindah ke Jakarta. Tapi kenapa ya, remote working masih belum sepopuler itu di Indonesia? Padahal potensinya besar banget. Ini yang jadi misi aku sekarang: mempopulerkan remote working di Indonesia. Soalnya, jujur aja, aku kadang sebel kalau lagi hiring remote worker. Isinya Filipina lagi, India lagi. Mana nih orang Indonesia-nya? Kita nggak boleh ketinggalan, Guys. Kita harus bisa bersaing di kancah global. Dengan skill dan talenta yang kita punya, harusnya kita bisa unjuk gigi. Bayangin deh, kalau makin banyak orang Indonesia yang kerja remote untuk perusahaan luar negeri. Pengangguran berkurang, ekonomi daerah tergerak, kesenjangan Jakarta-daerah bisa dipersempit. Apalagi, dengan kerja remote, kita bisa dapat exposure ke best practice dan budaya kerja yang lebih maju. Nggak cuma duit, tapi ilmu dan pengalaman kita juga nambah. Terus, yang paling penting, kita bisa tetap dekat dengan keluarga dan akar budaya kita. Nggak perlu jauh-jauh merantau ke luar negeri atau ke Jakarta. desc: Let’s go to Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿! From cruises to bus tours this year, I’m discovering that you don’t have to be simply one type of traveller - you can enjoy so many different kinds! And that’s super fun!        📍Save this Wales travel guide for your future adventures - and don’t forget to check out @rabbies_tours who do tours throughout all of the UK + and even in Europe! desc: 🌟 No one is coming to save you For the longest time, I kept waiting - waiting to feel ready, waiting for an opportunity to land in my lap. Even when you have little kids running all over you and a house to take care of. No one else is going to do it for you. desc: Я уже почти 3 года живу в Нячанге и уверена, что Вьетнам - самая опасная страна для переезда! И вот почему я так считаю: 1. Здесь неприлично дешево! И это ловушка. После Вьетнама любая страна кажется дорогой. Когда мы задумываемся о переезде, нам становится страшно от цен в других странах. От такой стоимости жизни сложно отказаться и многие остаются здесь на года, даже если приехали всего на месяц. 2. Идеальная погода. В Нячанге лето круглый год. Тут можно купаться и загорать даже зимой. Да, иногда бывают дожди, но они не идут неделями и никак не влияют на ритм жизни. Я больше не могу представить себя живущей в холодном климате. Ведь теперь даже +25 повод надеть кофту. 3. Невероятное разнообразие фруктов. Я так привыкла, что в моем рационе каждый день есть манго, папайя, авокадо и другие экзотические фрукты, что я уже не могу представить жизнь без этого. И это только малая часть того, почему я не могу решиться на переезд в другую страну. Будьте осторожны, приезжая во Вьетнам вы, возможно, уже не сможете уехать! #жизньвовьетнаме #жизньвнячанге #переездвазию #вьетнамопасен #ловушкавьетнама #жизньуморя #вечное лето #дешевоивкусно #реальныйвьетнам #VietnamLife #DigitalNomadLife #ForeverSummer #Vietnam #NhaTrang

stickersText:
Paying it fwd — this how 
we moved to Spain 🇪🇸 , The pathway is called 
DIGITAL NOMAD VISA
—
na launch ang visa na to nung 
2023 para sa mga non-eu 
remote workers na balak 
magstay sa Spain, upon initial 
approval they will grant you a 
short term resident visa (valid 
for 1 year) if sa Pinas ka mag 
apply, pwede syang irenew 
hanggang 5 years, We processed our application at the 
Spanish consulate in Manila last year 
March 2024.

Pinaka unang ginawa namin ay 
kumuha ng NIE appointment and then 
we prepared all the documents related 
to our remote job —
the list of requirements is published in 
the official Spanish Ministry of Foreign 
Affairs website. This visa is for remote 
workers/freelancers/ VA and the good 
thing is pwede mo agad dalhin ang 
family mo as long as you meet the 
requirements lalo na the income. , Nung na complete na namin lahat 
ng requirements including the 
translations and medical tests, we 
flew to Manila again and this time 
for our visa processing May 2024 —  
after 10 days we received a text na 
nadispatch na ang passport namin 
through LBC. 

The entire process took us 3 
months and we finally flew to Spain 
August 1, 2024

When we arrived here, nag reapply 
agad for resident permit through 
UGE and were granted 3 years 
residency., The biggest benefit of this 
visa is pwede ka agad mag 
apply ng citizenship after 2 
years of residency. 

Your family members/
dependents can also go to 
school (public for free) and 
your spouse can work locally.

As a tax and SS payer you are

desc: A lil recap of a realistic day in our life as digital nomads living in Valencia: – No commute, because we chose to stay in the city & we can work from anywhere – Some days we work from home, other days from a café (depends on the mood) – A balance of cooking at home and still eating out – Getting our steps in is easy because we prioritized staying in a walkable city – And we try our best to support local 🍎 We’re aware of the rising cost of living driven by nomads & expats so if you’re living this lifestyle too: please support local whenever you can 🫶🏼 Our sabbatical ended… but we didn’t want the travel to end with it. So we figured we should try and experience this nomadic life and the flexibility is incredibly freeing, but like everything it comes with his own challenges: - constantly planning our next move  - rebuilding a routine in every new place  - our bodies adapting to new food / environments  - making new friends / community It’s not easy but we love the freedom, growth and the perspective we’re gaining from it ✨🫶🏼 Would you consider working remotely and travelling?! #valencialife #digitalnomads #slowtravel #dayinthelife #remoteworklife #euro #eurosummer #travelcouple #travel #valencia #dayinalife #vlog #europe

stickersText:
How to Become a 
Digital Nomad 
in Spain 🇪🇸
(For Filipinos!), 👋 Hola amigos! 
John and Karen here, 
with our furbabies 
Chippy and Peewee 🐶🐶 
sharing how we Filipinos 
can live and work remotely 
in Spain 🇪🇸 through the 
Digital Nomad Visa 
or DNV 💻, 📍 Step 1: 📍
Prepare Your 
Remote Work Proof, ✅ You must work remotely 
for a company or clients 
outside Spain like 
US, UK, or PH clients., ✅ You must have worked 
with your current employer 
or freelance clients for 
at least 3 months., ✅ The company or clients 
must have been operating 
for at least 1 year., 📍 Step 2: 📍
Meet the 2025 
Income Requirement , Your income must be based 
on Spain’s minimum wage (SMI), 
which increases yearly by 
around 3–5%., 👉 For 2025, SMI = €1,381.50/month, 📊 Breakdown:
   - 🧑 Main Applicant: 200% of SMI 
                            → €2,763/month
   - 👩 First Dependent: +75% of SMI 
                            → +€1,036.13/month
   - 👶 Each Additional Dependent: +25% of SMI 
                            → +€345.38/month, Example: If you’re applying with 
your spouse and one child, your total 
income requirement is around €4,144/month., 📍 Step 3:📍
Gather Your Documents, 📑 Valid Passport

📑 Proof of income & remote work contract

📑 Bank statements (3–6 months)

📑 Private Health Insurance (valid in Spain)

📑 NBI Clearance (apostilled)

📑 Diploma or professional proof, 📍 Step 4: 📍
Apply for the Visa, 🇵🇭 Option 1: Apply through the 
Spanish Consulate in Manila

🇪🇸 Option 2: Enter Spain with a 
Schengen Visa, then apply directly to 
UGE (Unidad de Grandes Empresas), 💡 Many Filipinos choose Option 2, 
kasi mas mabilis once you’re 
already in Spain!, 📍 Step 5: 📍
Once Approved!, You’ll get 
3 years residence
as a Digital Nomad! 
🎉🎉🎉, Then you can:
🏡 Rent long-term
🏦 Open a bank account
💳 Get your TIE card
📱 Register as autónomo, 📍 Step 6: 📍
Bring Your Family, 👩‍❤️‍👨 Your spouse and kids
can also apply as dependents 
under your DNV.
(This step usually can be 
together with step 3 
with gathering the documents), ✨ “And that’s it! 
You can live, work, 
and travel 
legally in Spain 
as a Filipino 
remote worker 
🇪🇸💻🌍, ‼️Follow us for more Digital Nomad 
Visa tips and life here in Spain!

desc: Best Places to live in Southeast Asia for Digital Nomads 10. Georgetown, Malaysia 🇲🇾 Penang is the most vibrant island in Malaysia, very car centric but English speaking locals, great food and infrastructure and an upcoming Digital Nomad scene. 9. Siem Reap, Cambodia 🇰🇭 Siem Reap has some fantastic coworking hostels and cute cafés near Pub Street where you can peacefully work. And in your free time you can see some stunning temples too! 8. Ho-Chi-Minh-City, Vietnam 🇻🇳 Great cafe and coworking space scene and fun nightlife. Really fun city once you are able to manage the traffic. 😅 7. Ko Phangan, Thailand 🇹🇭 The spot for Digital Nomads in Thailand who search beach vibes. Big Digital Nomad community, great food options, but I felt like the island does not have too much to offer compared to other places on the list. 6. Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia Some of the best value for accommodation, feels more modern, clean and safe than other parts of SEA. 5. Chiang Mai, Thailand 🇹🇭 With all the convenience of Thailand but with cheaper prices than Ko Phangan. Only big downside is air quality. 4. Siargao, Philippines 🇵🇭 Beautiful island and very easy to make good friends with both locals and foreigners. Growing Digital Nomad scene and not as crowded as Bali yet. 3. Da Nang, Vietnam 🇻🇳 One if not the cheapest big city in Southeast Asia to live, which is the main pull here. And you have great food and a fantastic beachside in your backyard. 2. Bali, Indonesia 🇮🇩 The biggest Digital Nomad community, endless amount of stuff to do and inspiring people to meet. Never gets boring, only the traffic sucks. 1. Bangkok, Thailand 🇹🇭 One of the best connected places on Earth, you can get everything here, feels safe, great community of expats locals and good nightlife. #southeastasia #bangkok #bali #siargao #thailand #indonesia #digitalnomad #traveltips
